GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The export pipeline already has a perfect renderer for this document — the webview itself — and every export surface (styled HTML, PDF, print) flows through one HTML string produced by muya's ExportHtml.generate(). CSS, KaTeX and pele diagrams are inlined there already; raster images are the single remaining externality. Embedding them at export time is therefore a small, local completion of the existing design, not a new pipeline. The pass lives renderer-side because muya is a standalone DOM library with no file IO by contract (its theme CSS is read by the renderer, util/pdf.js, for the same reason), and the renderer already owns both the document's path context (currentFile) and the binary read primitive (ipcFs.readBinary + arrayBufferToBase64; readBinary already serves the shim's image loader). The detached-container DOM pass mirrors printService.renderMarkdown's existing image fix, so the pattern is proven in this codebase. The cap (8 MiB per image, raw file size) sits at the "email attachment" class: big enough for any reasonable screenshot or photo, small enough that one accidental giant TIFF cannot turn the .html into a 40 MB base64 blob.

Alternatives.Alternative: Inline inside muya's ExportHtml.generate() — rejected on layering: muya has no file-IO channel, would need a new injection point (options callback or window global reach-through), and the theme-CSS precedent already established that file IO belongs to the renderer.
Post-process the already-saved file on disk — same work plus a rewrite cycle and worse error surfacing; the DOM pass before save keeps one write and one notice path.
Fetch and inline remote http(s) images too — deferred: it adds network failure modes, changes export timing, and silently bundles third-party content; can be an opt-in later if the owner wants it.
A "self-contained" toggle in the export dialog — deferred: default-on with a skipped-count notice is honest without new UI; a toggle can be added later without breaking anything.

Broader export-quality work (Paged.js page numbers for PDF, a typst channel via the existing pandoc bridge) — separate changes from the same 2026-10-21 research conversation; this bundle deliberately does only image embedding.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Remote-image embedding (opt-in) and a user-configurable cap — revisit after owner reaction to the default-on behavior.

Whether the print/PDF container should also consume embedded data-URLs instead of its own src resolution — only if a real PDF image defect is reported; today that path is believed working and is regression-pinned instead.

Discovered by the review passes, outside this bundle's scope: the GitHub-image uploader reads images through the UTF-8 text channel (window.fileUtils.readFile → mt_fs_read) and therefore corrupts binary image bytes in the Tauri build — a separate defect-fix bundle should migrate it to ipcFs.readBinary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Owner exports a doc whose images live next to the .md, sends the single .html over Telegram; recipient opens it anywhere and sees every image.

A doc with a missing image (file deleted after editing) exports successfully; the recipient sees the one broken image exactly as the author would, and the author saw a "3 of 4 images embedded" notice at export time.

C-1.Name: Relative local PNG
C-1.Expected: Saved .html img src = data:image/png;base64,...; decoded bytes equal the fixture file; the file renders standalone from a directory without the images.

C-2.Name: Absolute POSIX path (/shot.png)
C-2.Expected: Normalized via correctImageSrc semantics, read from disk, embedded; original absolute path appears nowhere in the output.

C-3.Name: Windows path forms (\shot.png, \\?\\shot.png, generic \\server\share\shot.png)
C-3.Expected: Drive-letter and \\?\ extended-prefix forms normalize (isWin-gated, matching muya's correctImageSrc) and embed; generic UNC \\server\share matches no normalization branch anywhere in muya and passes through unchanged, uncounted.

C-4.Name: Percent-encoded and spaced src (my%20file.png, unicode имя.png)
C-4.Expected: Decoded before the filesystem read; embedded; no double-encoding in the data-URL.

C-5.Name: Remote http(s) image
C-5.Expected: src untouched in the output; zero network requests during export (pinned by the unit test's fetch/socket stub).

C-6.Name: Existing data: URL and pele inline SVG
C-6.Expected: Untouched by the pass; diagrams still render standalone (C-55 behavior preserved).

C-7.Name: Missing local image
C-7.Expected: Original src kept; counted skipped; export succeeds; notice reports k of n embedded.

C-8.Name: Image ≥ 8 MiB
C-8.Expected: Kept as original src; counted skipped; no base64 blow-up; notice reports it.

C-9.Name: Untitled document with a relative image
C-9.Expected: No document directory exists: src passes through unchanged, not counted, no crash, export succeeds.

C-10.Name: Same image referenced three times
C-10.Expected: One disk read; three identical data-URLs; skipped/total accounting counts references, not reads.

C-11.Name: Unknown extension (diagram.tiff)
C-11.Expected: Left as original src; counted skipped; never inlined with a guessed MIME.

C-12.Name: PDF/print regression guard
C-12.Expected: handleExport pdf and print branches never invoke the embedding pass; print-export.spec.ts expectations unchanged; print container still resolves src its own way.

Correctness.Note: Single funnel: only the styledHtml branch of handleExport calls the pass, so pdf/print cannot regress by construction (plus the pinned regression test). Path semantics reuse muya's correctImageSrc (the same normalization the print container relies on), so resolution rules are not forked. The pass runs after muya's DOMPurify sanitize and only rewrites img src values — no re-sanitization, no markup synthesis. Accounting counts references (what the user sees) while IO dedups by resolved path (what the disk sees); both numbers are needed by the notice, and the spec says which is which.

Security.Note: No new IPC surface, capability, or backend command: the read channel (ipcFs.readBinary → mt::fs::read_binary) is the one the shim's image loader already uses, and it can only open paths the renderer already handles. The document author's own local images becoming portable is the feature, not a leak — the output contains exactly what the document references. Remote images are deliberately not fetched, so export makes no outbound requests and cannot bundle third-party content silently. The 8 MiB cap bounds memory during base64 conversion. The skipped-count notice carries numbers only, never paths, per the repo console-privacy convention.

UX.Note: No new dialog or settings: default-on matches what "Export HTML" already promises (CSS and diagrams are inlined silently today — images joining them is consistency, not surprise). Honesty on partial output: a silent file with broken images is the current defect, so the skipped case gets a localized count notice in all ten locales; the success notice stays untouched. Untitled documents degrade gracefully instead of nagging — relative images there are unresolvable by construction and were broken in every previous version too.

Performance.Note: Cost is O(number of distinct local images): one sequential read each, bounded by the 8 MiB cap per image; typical documents (single-digit to a few dozen images) complete in well under a second, and the pass runs once per export click, not per keystroke. Dedup prevents re-reading repeated references. No watchers, no persistent state, no background work; memory spike is the base64 of one image at a time plus the final string. Output size grows by ~4/3 of the embedded images — inherent to data-URLs; the cap bounds each image, not the total (a hundred-image document can still produce a large file — a total cap is a NonGoal and a deferred decision), and the size is visible to the user as a file property before they send it.

Review.Findings: Pass A (correctness and GRACE contracts) and pass B (security, verification, UX) both returned FINDINGS with one shared major defect: the spec's load-bearing assumption that window.fileUtils.readFile returns binary was false — it routes to mt_fs_read and returns a UTF-8 string (a PNG would be lossily decoded), and the cited "proof" (the GitHub-uploader path, fileSystem.js:339-345) is itself latently corrupting in the Tauri build. Both passes independently identified the correct existing binary channel: ipcFs.readBinary (mt::fs::read_binary, Vec<u8>, MAX_READ_BYTES 10 MiB, already used by the shim's image loader) — the no-new-IPC constraint stays satisfiable. Spec corrected: R-6, Constraint 1 and the assumptions now name readBinary; the false readFile claim is gone. Minor findings also fixed: correctImageSrc is not exported through the muya barrel and yields file:// URLs behind an isWin gate — the spec now states the normalization is re-expressed in the util, scopes Windows forms to drive-letter/\\?\ (generic UNC passes through uncounted), and names the scheme strip; the owner quote in Problem is translated to English per the language policy; the Performance note no longer implies a total-size bound. Verified clean by both passes: exportHtml.js does no image rewriting today; the styledHtml-only scoping against editor.vue's three branches; printService renderStatic as the PDF-side resolver; DF-007/graph anchors; strict-contract compliance; notice privacy (counts only); runnable verification commands; ten-locale convention; the print-export.spec.ts regression pin; tauri-shim save/readBinary fixtures supporting the e2e assertion. The adjacent uploader defect is recorded above in DeferredDecisions for a separate bundle.
